title: Holistic dependency fuse with staged autorecovery and safe routing arbiter
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a coordinated "holistic dependency fuse" that evaluates failure signals across model, dependency, and tenant dimensions and triggers staged safe degradations. The fuse coordinates trip decisions using a short-term signal window and a longer error-budget burn indicator, then hands control to a 'safe routing arbiter' that applies an ordered fallback chain (cache -> lower-capacity model variant -> degraded endpoint -> soft-shed) with per-tenant SLAs enforced. This ticket covers algorithm design, runtime integration, observability, and rollout controls (canary, kill-switch, progressive expansion).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Fuse evaluates composite signals (5-min failure rate, 5-min p99 latency, resource pressure) and emits a single trip state that downstream routing consumers can subscribe to.
A2: Safe routing arbiter accepts policy config and executes ordered fallback chain with explicit TTLs and rollback windows.
A3: New metrics exposed: fuse_state, fuse_trip_reason, fuse_scope (model|dependency|tenant), staged_recovery_phase, fallback_action, fallback_latency_impact.
A4: End-to-end synthetic test demonstrates failover from hosted model to cached response within SLO window with no more than 2x latency observed for 95% of requests.
A5: Runbook and dashboard created; playbooks for manual override and GRACEful rollback documented and tested in staging.
A6: Controlled rollout plan (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on regression signals implemented.
A7: Integration tests for multi-region leader election and cross-region state quorum completed and passing in CI.
A8: No regression in baseline throughput or 99th percentile latency for non-impacted tenants during canary.
A9: Security review not required for initial implementation; later private deployment review gate added to roadmap.
A10: PRs: design doc and runtime changes merged to staging; perf benchmarks attached.
notes: Design rationale: single fuse reduces conflicting trips across different dimensions and prevents thrashing when multiple monitors fire concurrently.
Trip logic: two-layer decision — fast window (5m) uses weighted error-rate + p99 latency; slow window (1h) monitors error-budget burn and sustained resource pressure before hard isolation.
Staged autorecovery phases: QUARANTINE -> SOFT_RESTORE -> HOLD -> FULL_REINTEGRATION. Each phase has backoff timers and verification checks (synthetic traffic + live success sampling).

Fallback chain: cache lookup with TTL-awareness -> q4 model variant (lower compute/quantized) -> degraded endpoint (reduced context/prefix trimming) -> priority queueing with drop-after timeout -> shed.
Per-tenant controls: tenants can opt into aggressive safe-fallback policies or strict SLA-preserving policies via console flags. Default is SLA-preserving for enterprise customers.
Observability: tagging traces with fuse_state and fallback_action; add per-route dashboards and alerting on 'staged_recovery_phase != NONE' and 'fallback_rate > 0.5%'.

Trade-offs considered: global fuse vs localized fuses. We chose a federated fuse that elects a local leader per-region and surfaces a reconciled state to global control plane to avoid cross-region latencies while preserving consistent behavior.
Performance targets from load tests: trip should activate within 90s of sustained 5-min failure window breach and engage safe fallback within next request if cache hit available.
Rollback plan: emergency kill-switch in Console to force fuse to 'disabled' and route all traffic to primary model; metrics will be frozen and immediate rollback executed.
Implementation note: runtime changes live in gateway-router and runtime policy engine. Requires schema bump for routing-policy config and a lightweight subscription API for fuse state.
Docs: initial design doc at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/HD-Fuse-Design and draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1982
